fixtures.name: simple-turn
fixtures.quirk: one user turn and one complete assistant turn with full usage, preceded by a `permission-mode` control record

fixtures.name: multi-block-turn
fixtures.quirk: four assistant records share one `message.id` and one `requestId`; only the first carries the usage payload

fixtures.name: multi-block-turn-no-request-id
fixtures.quirk: assistant records omit `requestId` but share one `message.id`, which is the fallback request identity

fixtures.name: padded-request-id
fixtures.quirk: two request ids differ only by surrounding whitespace and must remain distinct grouping keys

fixtures.name: multi-record-request
fixtures.quirk: two assistant records copy one request's usage, which prompt attribution must charge exactly once

fixtures.name: multi-record-bad-copy
fixtures.quirk: one request has a readable usage copy and an unreadable sibling, so its measurement is disputed

fixtures.name: multi-record-broken-sibling
fixtures.quirk: one request record has broken ancestry while a sibling establishes both ownership and usage

fixtures.name: interleaved-turns
fixtures.quirk: two assistant messages interleave their blocks instead of arriving contiguously

fixtures.name: incomplete-then-complete
fixtures.quirk: a complete assistant message is followed by an in-progress one (`stop_reason: null`)

fixtures.name: files-touched
fixtures.quirk: two Read tool uses and a Grep in one assistant message — three calls, no file mutated

fixtures.name: retry-loop
fixtures.quirk: the same Bash command is retried four times, every attempt returning `is_error: true`

fixtures.name: consecutive-failures
fixtures.quirk: three different tools fail back to back, each with its own errored tool_result

fixtures.name: edit-revert
fixtures.quirk: an Edit is applied and then reverted; tool_results carry pre/post file hashes

fixtures.name: missing-output-tokens
fixtures.quirk: usage carries `input_tokens` only — `output_tokens` is absent, which is not the same as zero

fixtures.name: user-turn-blocks
fixtures.quirk: user records carrying tool_result blocks of very different sizes, one of them errored

fixtures.name: compact-boundary
fixtures.quirk: a `system` record with `subtype: compact_boundary` splits the transcript

fixtures.name: sidechain-turn
fixtures.quirk: every record is `isSidechain: true` in a primary `<session>.jsonl` — inline Task traffic, still its session's transcript

fixtures.name: sidechain-leading-then-main
fixtures.quirk: sidechain records precede the first main-chain record in the same file

fixtures.name: nested-subagent
fixtures.quirk: a subagent spawns a subagent, in one file, joined by `agentId`

fixtures.name: system-subagent-notification
fixtures.quirk: a `system`/`subagent_completed` record reports a child session id the transcript never contains

fixtures.name: task-notification
fixtures.quirk: Task tool notifications arrive as their own records

fixtures.name: slash-command-triad
fixtures.quirk: a slash command expands into a `<command-name>`/`<command-message>`/`<command-args>` triad of user records

fixtures.name: replacement-meta
fixtures.quirk: edit metadata only reaches the log on the tool_result, not on the tool_use

fixtures.name: oversized-bash-output
fixtures.quirk: an 80 KB Bash tool_result — the byte size is the fact, and no record is pretty-printed

fixtures.name: resume-marker
fixtures.quirk: the first user record is a `/resume <sessionId>` marker naming the prior session

fixtures.name: parent-chain-out-of-order
fixtures.quirk: records arrive out of `parentUuid` order, so turn grouping cannot rely on file order

fixtures.name: parent-chain-interrupt-resume
fixtures.quirk: an interrupted turn is resumed, and both halves hang off the same parent record

fixtures.name: original-session
fixtures.quirk: the root transcript that the fork and continuation fixtures point back at

fixtures.name: cross-file-parent-reconciliation
fixtures.quirk: a continuation whose first record's `parentUuid` only exists in the other file — the link is cross-file, not in-file

fixtures.name: explicit-continuation-reconciliation
fixtures.quirk: a continuation that states `continuedFromSessionId` on the record itself

fixtures.name: fork-reconciliation
fixtures.quirk: two transcripts share one source session id: a fork, not a continuation

fixtures.name: settings-reference
fixtures.quirk: burn's Claude settings input that sets the Bash output cap; relayhistory reads no settings file, so it is kept for provenance only

fixtures.name: summary-record
fixtures.quirk: a `type: "summary"` record with a `leafUuid` between two ordinary turns

fixtures.name: system-reminder
fixtures.quirk: `<system-reminder>` blocks injected into user content, as a block of their own, inline in a string prompt, and alone on an `isMeta` record

fixtures.name: hook-and-passthrough
fixtures.quirk: a `<user-prompt-submit-hook>` row flagged `isMeta`, a `<bash-input>` / `<bash-stdout>` pass-through pair, and a bare `isMeta` bookkeeping row between two prompts

fixtures.name: sidecar-subagent
fixtures.quirk: a subagent transcript in `<sessionId>/subagents/agent-<id>.jsonl` with its `agent-<id>.meta.json` sidecar, carrying the PARENT's sessionId

fixtures.name: nested-sidecars
fixtures.quirk: two `subagents/` sidecars whose meta files name no model: `a1` spawned from the main transcript, `a2` spawned by a tool use inside `a1` (`spawnDepth` 2); the spawn results carry `toolUseResult.agentId` on the record
